name: First results from the LUX dark matter experiment at the Sanford Underground Research Facility
notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.

summary.plain: In its first run (85.3 live days, April to August 2013), LUX saw data consistent with background only and set 90% confidence limits on dark matter scattering. The authors say the data disagree with low-mass dark matter interpretations of several other experiments' results, and that the limit is a significant improvement over earlier searches' sensitivities.
summary.technical: WS2013: 85.3 live days, 118 kg fiducial volume, April-August 2013. Data consistent with the background-only hypothesis; minimum 90% CL spin-independent WIMP-nucleon cross-section upper limit 7.6 × 10⁻⁴⁶ cm² at 33 GeV/c². The paper reports the data to be in disagreement with low-mass WIMP signal interpretations of the results from several recent direct detection experiments.

title: First results from the LUX dark matter experiment at the Sanford Underground Research Facility
why_it_matters: The paper states that its limit is a significant improvement over the sensitivities of earlier searches and that the LUX data are in disagreement with low-mass WIMP signal interpretations of the results from several recent direct detection experiments.
